newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices retain gains on mill buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices retain gains on mill buying.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Friday retained gains after fresh mill buying and low supplies sent prices up, dealers said.
"Spinning mills remained active buyers," one broker said.
Mills are buying cotton to make yarn for export.

In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned rose by 10 rupees at 1,810/1,850 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi rose by five rupees at 1,000/1,050 rupees per maund. Gujarat Kalyan also rose by 200 rupees at 14,000/14,400 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"Local demand for fabric and yarn however remained slow but export demand for yarn has prompted buying of cotton by the spinning mills," the broker said.

Long-staple Gujarat Sankar-4 was steady at 17,500/18,000 rupees per candy for the average variety and at 20,000/20,500 rupees for the superior variety. Overall volume remained slow during the day and sentiment was steady at the close of the session.
